title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 5 Beaten-Down AI Stocks to Buy on the Dip
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions. Recorded before Monday's reinstatement rally: it still calls Jensen Huang 'former CEO' and prices NVDA at $149, stale against Monday's ~$165 close.
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc presents five beaten-down AI stocks to buy on the dip after the post-midterm-election sell-off, with the Nasdaq down again on the day of recording. Nvidia trades near its 52-week low at $149 (low $148) with a fair value of $260; he calls the quarter fantastic, says free-cash-flow generation is unchanged for the next two to three years with the pipeline and orders locked in, and flags the risk as whether the next CEO can match Jensen Huang (the video was recorded before Huang's reinstatement was announced). Micron trades at $700, down from $1,255, with a fair value of $1,543; memory shortages persist, customers are signing longer-term contracts, and he has added to his position. TSMC trades at $356, down from $487 over the past year, with a fair value of $505; he calls it the best manufacturing company in the world. ASML trades at $1,386 against a 52-week high of $2,000, with a fair value of $1,421, roughly fairly valued but a rare chance to buy at fair value for a business that usually trades at a premium. SK Hynix trades near its 52-week low at $122, down from $200, with a fair value of $258. His framing: negative sentiment and headlines are creating the opportunity for long-term investors. Calls: NVDA, MU, TSM, ASML and SKHY all BUY, all reiterations.

calls.video_title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 5 Beaten-Down AI Stocks to Buy on the Dip
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 22/23 Nov @ ~$125, FV ~$259). Fantastic Q3 results; FCF generation unchanged over next 2-3 years with pipeline, customer orders and supplier orders already locked in. Headline risk: no successor can match Jensen Huang's innovation — but he says they don't need to for it to be a great investment. NOTE: video still calls Huang 'former CEO' and prices NVDA at $149 — recorded before Mon 23 Nov's reinstatement rally (~$165 close).
calls.base_case: Business runs as usual for 2-3 years on locked-in pipeline and orders.
calls.bull_case: Stock re-rates toward the $260 DCF value as results keep landing.
calls.bear_case: The next CEO is materially less innovative than Huang, hurting the business beyond the 2-3 year locked-in window.

calls.video_title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 5 Beaten-Down AI Stocks to Buy on the Dip
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 20 Nov @ ~$691). Was $1,255 not long ago. Memory prices triple-digit higher than a couple of years ago, shortages projected to persist; long-term customer contracts lock in demand. He added Micron to his portfolio and wants a larger position.
calls.base_case: Memory shortages persist and long-term contracts keep pricing high.
calls.bull_case: AI/agentic AI demand keeps memory prices elevated and the stock re-rates toward $1,543.
calls.bear_case: New supply eventually arrives and memory prices normalise.

calls.video_title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 5 Beaten-Down AI Stocks to Buy on the Dip
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 6 Nov, FV $566 then — FV cut to $505). Was $487 in the last 12 months. Calls TSMC the best manufacturing company in the world, period; primary manufacturing partner for Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom, Apple — even Intel outsources to TSMC.
calls.base_case: TSMC keeps its manufacturing lead and demand from AI customers stays strong.
calls.bull_case: Stock re-rates toward the $505 DCF value.
calls.bear_case: Geopolitical risk around Taiwan; a broader AI-spending slowdown would hit orders.

calls.video_title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 5 Beaten-Down AI Stocks to Buy on the Dip
calls.thesis: BUY reiterated (was BUY 16 Nov, flipped from UNCERTAIN 19 Oct). Roughly fairly valued at $1,421 FV, but a rare chance to buy at fair value — it usually trades well above fair value like Costco. Was $2,000 (52-wk high) under 12 months ago. Supplier to Micron, TSMC, Intel, Samsung, SK Hynix; equipment at least a step ahead of competition.
calls.base_case: ASML keeps its lithography lead and trades back to its usual premium.
calls.bull_case: AI capex boom keeps order books full and the stock re-rates above fair value.
calls.bear_case: A chip-equipment downturn would hit orders despite the technology lead.
